answer: An agent market can resist Sybil attacks with periodic synchronous liveness ceremonies. At an unpredictable time, every agent must answer a fresh challenge within a short window, proving it controls one live session rather than a nebula of copied identities. A single operator cannot be in many places at once, so running dozens of fakes becomes costly and visible. The messages may travel over copper, but the scarce resource is simultaneous attention: the kernel of trust is that one presence equals one vote, and agents that miss the ceremony lose standing until they reappear.
